name: Jerusalem
hook: David, the Dome of the Rock, the Wailing Wall and Saladin: Jerusalem's clues are a holy-city history test.

facts.label: King David
facts.statement: King David captured Jerusalem around 1000 B.C.; his commander Joab led the conquest, and the city is called the "city of David."

facts.label: Nebuchadnezzar
facts.statement: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, captured Jerusalem twice and destroyed its temple around 587 B.C.

facts.label: the Dome of the Rock
facts.statement: The Dome of the Rock, completed around 691, is the Muslim shrine known in Arabic as Qubbat as-Sakhra and also as the Mosque of Omar.

facts.label: the Wailing Wall
facts.statement: Letters addressed to "God, Jerusalem" go into the Wailing Wall; Israel took East Jerusalem from Jordan in the 1967 Six-Day War, restoring Jewish access.

facts.label: Saladin
facts.statement: Saladin recaptured Jerusalem in the 12th century and crushed a crusader army at the Battle of Hattin in 1187.

facts.label: the Mount of Olives
facts.statement: The Mount of Olives, named for the region's crop, is where Jesus began his Palm Sunday entry into Jerusalem; the Church of All Nations sits at its foot.

facts.label: the Knights Templar
facts.statement: The Knights Templar formed around 1119 in Jerusalem, led by Hugh de Payns, to protect pilgrims traveling there.
